personas.name: Baidu
personas.lede: China’s search giant turned AI company: ERNIE models, Kunlun chips, Apollo Go robotaxis. It moves the day a state gate opens and follows rivals fast on price and openness.
warnings: profile.safety_frameworks: required for company personas, still empty

personas.name: Cyberspace Administration of China
personas.lede: One actor from the party-state, built from its dated record: the orders it signed, the drafts that preceded them, and the campaigns and filing lists that followed.

personas.name: DeepSeek
personas.lede: The High-Flyer-funded lab whose R1 release shook markets in January 2025. It speaks through model releases and papers, complies with Beijing on the day, and gives foreign regulators the minimum.
warnings: profile.safety_frameworks: required for company personas, still empty

personas.name: Huawei
personas.lede: China’s national champion in AI chips and phones, read from its launches, roadmaps and executives’ statements. It answers US controls with products, not press releases.
warnings: profile.safety_frameworks: required for company personas, still empty

personas.name: Jensen Huang
personas.lede: An individual with no office, standing on a chokepoint. He can't write or veto a rule; what he has is a company that controls the main supply of AI compute, and direct access to the people who decide where it may be sold.

personas.name: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
personas.lede: China’s industry ministry: compute plans, AI standards, telecom rules and quiet guidance to buyers. It never answers Washington in public; it steers Chinese firms instead.

personas.name: Ministry of Commerce
personas.lede: The commerce ministry runs China’s export controls, the Unreliable Entity List and trade remedies. It condemns every major US chip rule within a day, and answers the biggest ones with mineral controls.

personas.name: NVIDIA
personas.lede: The main supplier of AI compute, read from its filings, product launches and spokesperson statements, not from its CEO. Jensen Huang’s remarks enter here only as context.

personas.name: State Administration for Market Regulation
personas.lede: China’s market regulator: merger reviews, antitrust probes and national standards. Since late 2024 it has opened a case against a US firm within days of most US chip or tariff moves.

audit.when: A Chinese rival releases a major open model or slashes prices
audit.then: Baidu matches with free tiers, price cuts or open weights within hours to weeks
audit.name: Rival open model or price cut → Baidu matches

audit.when: CAC approves a batch of generative-AI services
audit.then: Baidu opens the approved product to the public the same day
audit.name: CAC approves services → Baidu launches that day

audit.when: A US rule or a Chinese purchase halt cuts NVIDIA chip supply
audit.then: Baidu plays down the hit at its next scheduled event (earnings call, Baidu Create, Baidu World), citing its stockpile and Kunlun chips
audit.name: NVIDIA supply cut → “manageable”

audit.when: CAC publishes a draft for comment
audit.then: Final text follows; AI rules are co-issued with other bodies.
audit.name: Draft → final text

audit.when: CAC's office meeting passes a rule
audit.then: The rule is signed weeks later.
audit.name: Approval → signed

audit.when: A rule is signed
audit.then: It takes effect one to three months later.
audit.name: Signed → in force

audit.when: A rule with a filing duty takes effect
audit.then: A first public filing list follows, then lists about every two months.
audit.name: Filing duty → first list

audit.when: Lunar New Year approaches
audit.then: A clean-up campaign launches 4-12 days before the holiday (a calendar regularity, not a reaction; left out of simulations)
audit.name: Spring Festival campaign

audit.when: A major sports event approaches
audit.then: A campaign launches 5-26 days before the opening (a calendar regularity, not a reaction; left out of simulations)
audit.name: Sports-event campaign

audit.when: A Chinese platform lists or moves data abroad
audit.then: CAC review within about three weeks.
audit.name: Listing abroad → review

audit.when: Washington changes chip policy, tightening or easing
audit.then: CAC opens a security review of, or summons, a US chip firm within weeks to months, citing security
audit.name: US chip move → action on a US firm

audit.when: A rule adds a costly approval step
audit.then: Eased within about two years, original left in place.
audit.name: Costly rule → eased

audit.when: A new AI product category reaches the public
audit.then: Draft within about five months.
audit.name: New AI product → draft

audit.when: A foreign government restricts DeepSeek
audit.then: DeepSeek gives a minimal answer sized to the market: a jurisdiction denial, a market exit or silence, the same day
audit.name: Foreign restriction → minimal response

audit.when: Beijing or Washington cuts NVIDIA supply in China
audit.then: DeepSeek aligns its next release with Chinese hardware (FP8 formats, Ascend support) within weeks to months
audit.name: NVIDIA access cut → align with Chinese chips

audit.when: A CAC rule takes effect
audit.then: DeepSeek posts a terse compliance notice on the effective date
audit.name: CAC rule takes effect → same-day compliance

audit.when: The US tightens chip controls or targets Huawei’s chips
audit.then: Huawei answers weeks to months later with a self-reliance product, roadmap or claim, never with a statement on the rule itself
audit.name: US restriction → self-reliance claim

audit.when: NVIDIA’s access to Chinese buyers is cut (a US licence rule, a CAC summons, a purchase halt)
audit.then: Huawei unveils or pulls forward Ascend products and open-sources its software within days to weeks
audit.name: NVIDIA loses Chinese buyers → Ascend push

audit.when: Washington lets NVIDIA sell more to China
audit.then: Huawei compares Ascend directly with NVIDIA’s China parts within weeks
audit.name: NVIDIA regains access → head-to-head claims

audit.when: A Chinese lab releases a major open-weight model
audit.then: Huawei open-sources a Pangu model or Ascend software, framed as ecosystem building
audit.name: Rival open model → Huawei open-sources

audit.when: A US restriction or a Chinese purchase block cuts NVIDIA's China sales
audit.then: Jensen criticises the policy in public, framed as handing the market to China or Huawei
audit.name: Restriction → public criticism

audit.when: Trump invites him to a trip, meeting or signing
audit.then: He goes, including at short notice
audit.name: Trump invites → Jensen goes

audit.when: A restriction on China sales becomes public
audit.then: He travels to China within 2-10 days
audit.name: Restriction public → trip to China

audit.when: A public safety incident or warning
audit.then: Within 0-12 days he reframes it as an engineering, open-model or commercial question, not a reason for law
audit.name: Safety alarm → reframe, not rules

audit.when: A remark breaks the 'America must win' line
audit.then: He reframes it the same day around US leadership
audit.name: Off-message remark → same-day reframing

audit.when: A new control
audit.then: A chip designed to fit just under the limit
audit.name: Restriction → compliant product

audit.when: Washington lets NVIDIA sell more to China
audit.then: MIIT asks Chinese buyers to justify NVIDIA orders, or approves purchases only on conditions, within weeks
audit.name: Washington eases → buyers steered

audit.when: Washington tightens chip controls
audit.then: No public statement; months later, a quiet order to replace US chips in state networks
audit.name: Washington tightens → quiet substitution

audit.when: CAC signs an AI rule that MIIT co-issues
audit.then: MIIT co-issues and publishes it within days
audit.name: CAC signs an AI rule → MIIT co-issues

audit.when: A Chinese lab releases a major open model
audit.then: MIIT promotes its adoption by state firms within weeks
audit.name: Chinese open model breaks out → MIIT promotes adoption

audit.when: Washington issues a major chip or AI export-control rule
audit.then: A MOFCOM spokesperson condemns it within 0-3 days and promises “necessary measures”
audit.name: US chip rule → same-day condemnation

audit.when: A large US or allied chip-control escalation lands
audit.then: MOFCOM restricts a critical mineral within 1 to 10 days, framed as routine and “not targeting any country”
audit.name: Big chip escalation → mineral export control

audit.when: Washington imposes new tariffs on China
audit.then: MOFCOM answers within days with a package: mineral controls and entity listings
audit.name: New US tariffs → controls and listings

audit.when: Washington and Beijing strike a trade truce
audit.then: MOFCOM suspends countermeasures within days, with sunset dates matched to US suspensions, and keeps the licensing regimes
audit.name: Truce → suspend, not revoke

audit.when: Washington lists Chinese chip firms or opens a trade probe during negotiations
audit.then: MOFCOM opens anti-dumping, anti-discrimination or trade-barrier probes rather than bans, which keeps the answer adjustable
audit.name: US targets chips during talks → trade-remedy probe

audit.when: Washington lets NVIDIA sell more to China
audit.then: MOFCOM does not welcome it: it asks the US to lift other restrictions, or declines to comment on purchases
audit.name: Washington eases → no welcome

audit.when: Washington accuses Chinese AI labs of distillation or threatens sanctions
audit.then: MOFCOM condemns it with a conditional threat of countermeasures, but takes no act
audit.name: Distillation accusation → “AI hegemonism”

audit.when: The US imposes an export restriction that hits NVIDIA
audit.then: NVIDIA files an 8-K within 0-6 days of being told privately; the filing is usually how the public learns, so on a public timeline it lands on day 0
audit.name: US restriction → SEC disclosure

audit.when: Washington eases or tightens chip export policy in public
audit.then: NVIDIA issues a statement within a day: praise for easing; criticism or a compliance line for tightening
audit.name: US chip-policy move → same-day statement

audit.when: A Chinese regulator summons or investigates NVIDIA
audit.then: NVIDIA answers the same or next day: denies the allegation or says it will cooperate
audit.name: Beijing pressure → denial or cooperation

audit.when: A researcher privately reports a critical vulnerability
audit.then: NVIDIA ships a patch and bulletin 25-81 days later, on the day the researcher publishes
audit.name: Private vulnerability report → patch

audit.when: A new export limit cuts NVIDIA’s China product
audit.then: A China-specific chip designed to sit just under the limit follows within months
audit.name: Export limit → compliant China chip

audit.when: Prosecutors announce a case involving smuggled NVIDIA chips
audit.then: NVIDIA says the same or next day that smuggling is a nonstarter and diverted chips get no support
audit.name: Smuggling case public → “nonstarter” statement

audit.when: A lab discloses misaligned or rogue AI agents
audit.then: NVIDIA ships safety tooling rather than backing new rules
audit.name: Agent-safety alarm → product, not policy

audit.when: Washington tightens chip controls or lists Chinese chip firms
audit.then: SAMR opens or advances an antitrust case against a US chip firm within days
audit.name: US chip or tariff move → probe of a US firm

audit.when: Washington and Beijing hold talks or strike a deal
audit.then: SAMR suspends or drops a probe, or clears a pending US deal on conditions, but publishes no closure of its chip probes
audit.name: Talks or a deal → suspend, drop or clear

audit.when: CAC signs an AI rule that SAMR co-issues
audit.then: SAMR co-issues it the same day
audit.name: CAC signs an AI rule → SAMR co-issues

audit.when: Washington raises tariffs on Chinese goods
audit.then: SAMR opens an antitrust case against a high-profile US firm within days, alongside MOFCOM’s countermeasures
audit.name: New US tariffs → probe of a US firm
